What longevity compounds does Blueberries contain, and which hallmarks of aging do they target? Please cite the evidence.

Blueberries (cup) contains 4 longevity-relevant compounds with verified hallmark links:

**Quercetin**: Cellular Senescence (evidence weight 0.60; PMID 36857968): Dasatinib + quercetin (D+Q) phase I feasibility/tolerability in IPF (eBioMedicine 2023; PMID 36857968)

**Resveratrol**: Deregulated Nutrient Sensing (evidence weight 0.85; PMID 22560220): SIRT1/AMPK-related signaling and mitochondrial stress-response biology (primary verified review anchor); Altered Intercellular Communication (evidence weight 0.35; PMID 34257808, PMID 33551004): NF-κB / inflammatory modulation proposed in resveratrol aging reviews (PMIDs queued for manual confirmation)

**Vitamin C (Ascorbic Acid)**: Genomic Instability (evidence weight 0.85; PMID 29099763): Vitamin C is a potent antioxidant that reduces oxidative DNA damage and supports DNA repair enzyme activity; Cellular Senescence (evidence weight 0.60; PMID 29099763): Vitamin C reduces oxidative stress-induced senescence and supports collagen synthesis in aging tissues; Altered Intercellular Communication (evidence weight 0.60; PMID 29099763): Vitamin C modulates immune cell function and reduces inflammatory cytokine production

**Pterostilbene**: Epigenetic Alterations (evidence weight 0.45; PMID 22304824): Pterostilbene activates SIRT1 and modulates DNA methylation patterns; superior bioavailability vs resveratrol; Deregulated Nutrient Sensing (evidence weight 0.45; PMID 22304824): Pterostilbene activates AMPK and SIRT1, modulating nutrient-sensing pathways in aging models; Genomic Instability (evidence weight 0.45; PMID 22304824): Pterostilbene reduces oxidative DNA damage via Nrf2 activation and antioxidant enzyme induction

Dietary note: Highest pterostilbene content of common berries; quercetin ~7.7mg/100g RUO — not medical advice.
